name: IL-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Mike Bost running with a large fundraising edge
Democratic challenger underfunded with minimal outside support
Prediction markets price Bost near certain to win
model.rationale: The R+22 district lean, Bost's incumbency, and his roughly 15-to-1 fundraising advantage over Julie Fortier all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and markets price a Bost win at about 96%. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, there is little reason to move from the fundamentals.
model.watch: A major late outside spending push for Fortier or an unexpected scandal involving Bost would be the main ways this race could tighten.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview: Mike Bost seeks another term in a southern Illinois district that leans heavily Republican, about 22 points toward the GOP at the baseline. He is a well-established incumbent with roughly $790,000 on hand after raising over $1.3 million. Democrat Julie Fortier has raised under $90,000 with about $60,000 available and no meaningful outside spending on either side. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the picture rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets give Bost about a 96% chance of winning. The combination of the district's strong partisan lean, incumbency, and a lopsided financial advantage makes this a safe Republican seat, with only a remote chance of an upset.
